title: Are Dogs a Shark's Favorite Meal?
summary: Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant discuss whether dogs are a shark's favorite meal, prompted by Josh's recurring nightmares about his dogs being eaten by sharks. They cover thalassophobia-style fear (named in the transcript as "gaiya phobia," likely galeophobia), the Jaws effect, shark attack and fatality statistics, bull sharks swimming up rivers as far north as Illinois on the Mississippi, and what sharks eat. The answer: dogs are not a shark's favorite meal, though mistaken identity is possible. Sharks prefer blubber; bull sharks bump-and-bite to test prey, and tiger sharks eat varied debris. The episode opens and closes with ad reads for the Camry and consumer sites.
topics: fear of being eaten by sharks

segments.title: Opening sponsor reads
segments.summary: Opening sponsor read for the Camry, then the show introduction by Josh Clark and Chuck Bryant.

segments.title: Banter and Josh's dog nightmares
segments.summary: Chuck asks about dogs. Josh says he sometimes wakes in a panic from dreams of his dogs being eaten by sharks, prompted by a 2005 article in the British tabloid The Sun about a dog used as shark bait with a hook through its nose.

segments.title: Fear of sharks and the Jaws effect
segments.summary: Chuck identifies the fear as galeophobia (fear of being eaten by a shark) and attributes its strength to the Jaws effect. They note shark attacks are rare: about seventy-one attacks across all species in 2007, with one fatality.

segments.title: Shark attack statistics in perspective
segments.summary: Chuck gives comparison figures: twelve people killed by sharks in the US between 1999 and 2006 versus sixteen killed by sand hole collapses, thirteen shark injuries in 2007, and over fifteen hundred human bite injuries in New York City alone that year.

segments.title: Bull sharks in fresh water
segments.summary: Discussion of bull sharks that swim up rivers and survive in fresh water, spotted as far north as Illinois on the Mississippi River.

segments.title: What sharks eat and whether dogs are on the menu
segments.summary: Josh answers that dogs are not a shark's favorite meal, though a shark may eat one by mistake. Bull sharks bump and bite to test prey and favor blubber; tiger sharks eat odd items like license plates and shoes; great whites bite gently to test prey and seals are a favorite.

segments.title: Sign-off and closing ad
segments.summary: Closing pitch pointing listeners to HowStuffWorks.com and an email address for feedback, followed by a closing sponsor read.
